summary: Alessandro Michele closed his first Valentino show in Rome with a full-length red dress whose V-shaped cutout at the back ran from shoulders to sacrum. It was both a salute to the late founder and an exhalation after a complex exercise. Speaking afterwards, Michele said: “I let the color go, because it has a presence. Red is very difficult to handle…. Here it is a sign that gives you chills when you see it.” Now nearly two years into his time at the house, Michele said he sees himself as an “interference” in the aesthetic edifice its founder constructed. “Valentino made those lessons perfect, and I am always a little crooked,” he said. This is why Interference was the name of the collection, and tension—whether associative, visual, or emotional—was what Michele wanted to generate. cm-unit The urgent frequency of his eclectic tastes signaled far more strongly in the looks that came before that last one. A bolstered, rounded shoulderline emanated high-1980s excess: From it Michele hung multiple versions of his glitched Valentino woman, sometimes accented with butterfly-shaped hardware that suggested the metamorphosis he was exploring. Bow-tied belts cinched full-length furs or cropped wrap leather coats with wide-action shoulders. Satin sash belts cut across color-block pleated tunics and over lace-hemmed jeans with Rockstud pumps. Whipped twists of double-faced taffeta were slung in swirls from the hip beneath more deep-V cutouts, this time at the front and framed in lace. The graphic zigzag of black-edged pink and ivory in a sequined full-sleeve jacket illustrated the ka-pow Michele was punching for. The menswear was less mixed, but no less subject to tension. From the front the double-breasted gray jacket in look five appeared almost banal, but at the back a harmony-busting vortex of drapery whirled like water pushed through a propeller. “I am always standing with two feet in two different places,” Michele said. “You must hold on, you must let go.” Full-legged trousers were shaped by purposefully mish-mashed pleating that might have been pressed either through design or dereliction; that ambiguity seemed the point. There was an abundance of almost ecclesiastical drape and fold that echoed the raiments painted by Cortona on the ceiling above us in Palazzo Barberini. In one of his notes (Michele luxuriates in rhetorical material as much as he does fabric) it was asserted that the collection “celebrates order while simultaneously revealing its own structural vulnerability”: the classic rise and fall. Surrounded by so much artistic and architectural history, and charged with carrying the torch for such a canonical emperor in the city’s fashion lore, Michele is teasing at glitches and running interference in order to place Valentino as just much in the now as it will forever be in the then.

mapping.note: Details matched to looks by Gemini vision inside a monotonic window, then globally aligned so parent look numbers never run backwards. Per-detail confidence and evidence are in 'detail_matches'.

detail_matches.evidence: The detail image perfectly matches Look 1, showing the same brown fur coat with auburn streaks, a black leather belt tied in a bow, and a delicate gold necklace with a small charm.
The model, the distinctive choker necklace, and the fuchsia top with black lace trim are identical in both the detail and Look 2.
The model, brown leather jacket with structured shoulders, multi-strand pearl necklace with green emerald pendant, and large chandelier earrings are all identical to the detail image.

The detail image shows the back of a long, olive-brown coat with a distinctive twisted and pleated design. Look 4 features the exact same coat, color, and unique back design, worn by a male model with similar hair and a matching striped shirt collar.
The model, sunglasses, grey blazer, and draped taupe undergarment are identical in both the detail and look 5.

The detail image perfectly matches Look 6, including the pink lace bodice, black velvet sleeves, light blue pleated cummerbund, multi-strand pearl necklace with emerald pendant, matching earrings, and the model's hair and makeup.
The detail image perfectly matches the patterned hosiery and the black ankle-strap heels with an orange toe and metallic heel from Look 6.
Exact match of black lace-trimmed garment, purple sheer hosiery, and light pink open-toe heels with gold heel.
The detail image perfectly matches the purple hosiery, the cream and red-toed high heels with an ankle strap, and the black lace trim on the sheer skirt of Look 8.

The detail image shows a pleated garment with an abstract pattern in brown, beige, purple, and gold, a black waist band, and a distinctive multi-strand cream beaded necklace with a large gemstone pendant. Look 9 features the identical pleated garment, waist band, and necklace.
The detail image perfectly matches Look 10, including the pink high-neck pleated top, the dark magenta pleated belt, the model's long wavy hair, and the long dangling silver earrings.
The detail image perfectly matches the teal suede heels with ankle strap and bow, the pink hosiery, and the sheer black skirt with lace trim seen in Look 11.

The detail shows a green draped top with a heavily embellished, ruched silver cuff, paired with a red satin-like skirt. Look 12 features a model with the same dark skin tone wearing an identical green draped top with the same embellished cuffs and a matching red flowing skirt.
The model's hair, sunglasses, and the distinctive pleated turquoise high-neck garment are identical in both the detail and Look 13.
The fur coat, blue jeans, and black chain-strap bag with the 'V' logo are identical in both images.
The model's skin tone and short hair match. The brown fur collar and the distinctive large, ornate silver-toned earrings with rhinestones and pearl drops are identical in both the detail and Look 15.
The detail image perfectly matches the purple hosiery, the light pink open-toe heels with an ankle bow, and the dark red draped fabric visible in Look 16.
The detail image perfectly matches Look 17, including the light pink top, the ruched purple skirt with a draped element, the purple hosiery, and the white studded high-heeled sandals.
